## PR title

`Force csv.reader fallback when a backslash appears in a row`

## PR body

```markdown
## Summary

The naive splitter in `csv_converter._split_row` skipped the csv.reader
fallback whenever the line contained no `"` character. RFC 4180 allows
backslash-escaped quote pairs inside quoted fields (`\"\"`), and rows
containing only that escape sequence — like `"foo\\"\"bar",baz` — slipped
through the fast path and crashed at the cell-merging step with an
IndexError.

## Root cause

`_split_row` was added as an optimization to avoid csv.reader's overhead
on simple rows. Its guard checked only for `"`, not for `\\`. Backslash
is a meta-character in csv.reader's parser; rows containing it must use
the full RFC 4180 path even when no top-level quote appears in the line.

## Fix

Add `\\` to the fast-path bailout condition. Both characters now force
the csv.reader fallback.

## Verification

Tested manually with the failing input.
```
